name: ADC.6

power.notes: About 5.6 mA typical: the STM32L011 running at 32 MHz (5.4 mA) plus the ADC and its 16 MHz clock. The tile never sleeps.

i2cAddress.label: I2C address
i2cAddress.description: The four addresses Studio can pick directly (driver instances 0-3). The tile stores any address from 0x08 to 0x77; set it with set_address and reach it with cfg.address.

options.label: Two output periods (nulls half the output rate: 50 Hz at 100 Hz out)

headline: six-channel analog input
description:
Sense.ADC.6 turns six analog inputs into calibrated millivolt readings served over I2C, so a host reads voltages instead of managing an ADC. All sampling, filtering and timing happen on the tile. It sweeps the six channels continuously at a paced rate and publishes a filtered set at a configurable output rate, 100 Hz by default.

Every published set is coherent: all six channels come from the same instant, never a mix of old and new, and each set carries a sequence number so a host can tell a fresh reading from a repeat. Readings span 0 V to the tile's own supply, which the tile measures against an internal reference at power-up and uses as full scale, rather than assuming it. The supply is readable too.

Inputs accept source impedances up to roughly 30–50 kΩ.  Output rate (1–250 Hz), sweeps averaged per period (1–32), and filter-window length are all settable at runtime and can be stored on the tile to survive reboot.

application_notes.details: The I2C address is stored on the tile and changeable across 0x08–0x77, so several tiles can share one bus; it ships at 0x28.
application_notes.heading: I2C address

application_notes.details: Filtering is a boxcar average whose window is set in output periods, which doubles as mains rejection: a two-period window nulls 50 Hz at a 100 Hz output, or 60 Hz at 120 Hz, and a 100 ms window nulls both
application_notes.heading: Filtering

application_notes.details: Poll a little faster than the output rate, two to three times, and use the sequence number to discard repeats. The tile's clock and the host's drift apart by about a percent, so polling at exactly the output rate will occasionally read the same set twice or miss one.
application_notes.heading: Polling
